import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sphere packing

A sphere packing in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a collection of unit balls with pairwise disjoint interiors,
i.e. a set $X$ of centers with $\|x - y\| \ge 2$ for all distinct $x, y \in X$. Its (upper)
density is
$$\Delta_X = \limsup_{R \to \infty}
  \frac{\operatorname{Vol}\big((\bigcup_{x \in X} B(x, 1)) \cap B(0, R)\big)}
       {\operatorname{Vol}(B(0, R))},$$
and the sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$ is the supremum of $\Delta_X$ over all packings $X$
in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Restricting to packings whose centers form a lattice gives the lattice packing
constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$.

The value of $\Delta_n$ is known only for $n = 1, 2, 3, 8, 24$, and $\Delta_n^{(L)}$ only for
$n \le 8$ and $n = 24$. This file records conjectures on the remaining cases and on the
asymptotic behaviour of $\Delta_n$ for large $n$:

- the Conway–Sloane conjecture $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for $n \le 9$ [Sl98];
- the conjecture that in some dimension the densest packing is irregular, i.e.
  $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$, and its strong form that this holds for all sufficiently large
  $n$ [CK09];
- the Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound
  $\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim 3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$ [TS06].

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sl98] Sloane, N. J. A., "The sphere-packing problem", Documenta Mathematica, Extra Volume
  ICM 1998, III, 387–396. [arXiv:math/0207256](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207256)
- [CS95] Conway, J. H., Sloane, N. J. A., "What are all the best sphere packings in low
  dimensions?", Discrete & Computational Geometry 13 (1995), 383–403.
- [CK09] Cohn, H., Kumar, A., "Optimality and uniqueness of the Leech lattice among lattices",
  Annals of Mathematics 170 (2009), 1003–1050.
  [arXiv:math/0403263](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0403263)
- [TS06] Torquato, S., Stillinger, F. H., "New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density
  of sphere packings", Experimental Mathematics 15 (2006), 307–331.
  [arXiv:math/0508381](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
- [Vi17] Viazovska, M., "The sphere packing problem in dimension 8", Annals of Mathematics 185
  (2017), 991–1015. [arXiv:1603.04246](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04246)
- [CKMRV17] Cohn, H., Kumar, A., Miller, S. D., Radchenko, D., Viazovska, M., "The sphere
  packing problem in dimension 24", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), 1017–1033.
  [arXiv:1603.06518](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06518)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry Filter MeasureTheory Metric Real

namespace SpherePacking

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A set `X` of points of `ℝ^n` is the set of centers of a packing of unit balls if any two
distinct points of `X` are at distance at least `2`, so that the open unit balls centered at the
points of `X` are pairwise disjoint. -/
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y ↦ 2 ≤ dist x y

/-- The finite density of the packing of unit balls with centers `X`: the fraction of the ball
of radius `R` about the origin covered by the unit balls centered at points of `X`. -/
noncomputable def finiteDensity (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (R : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  volume.real ((⋃ x ∈ X, ball x 1) ∩ ball 0 R) / volume.real (ball (0 : ℝ^n) R)

/-- The (upper) density $\Delta_X$ of the packing of unit balls with centers `X`: the limit
superior of its finite densities as the radius tends to infinity. -/
noncomputable def density (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : ℝ :=
  atTop.limsup (finiteDensity X)

/-- The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$: the supremum of the densities of all packings of
unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^n$. -/
noncomputable def spherePackingDensity (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X})

/-- A set `X` of points of `ℝ^n` is a lattice if it is a discrete additive subgroup of `ℝ^n`
spanning `ℝ^n`, i.e. the `ℤ`-span of a basis of `ℝ^n`. -/
def IsLattice (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L), IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ X = L

/-- The lattice packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$: the supremum of the densities of all packings
of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose centers form a lattice. -/
noncomputable def latticePackingDensity (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X ∧ IsLattice X})

/-- The empty set is a packing. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isPacking_empty : IsPacking (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) :=
  Set.pairwise_empty _

/-- The empty packing has density `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem density_empty : density (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = 0 := by
  have h : finiteDensity (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = fun _ ↦ 0 := by
    ext R
    simp [finiteDensity]
  rw [density, h, limsup_const]

/-- Finite densities are nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem finiteDensity_nonneg (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (R : ℝ) : 0 ≤ finiteDensity X R :=
  div_nonneg measureReal_nonneg measureReal_nonneg

/-- Finite densities are at most `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem finiteDensity_le_one (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (R : ℝ) : finiteDensity X R ≤ 1 :=
  div_le_one_of_le₀ (measureReal_mono Set.inter_subset_right) measureReal_nonneg

/-- The density of a packing is at most `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem density_le_one (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : density X ≤ 1 :=
  limsup_le_of_le (isBoundedUnder_of ⟨0, finiteDensity_nonneg X⟩).isCoboundedUnder_le
    (Eventually.of_forall (finiteDensity_le_one X))

/-- The sphere packing constant is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem spherePackingDensity_nonneg (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ spherePackingDensity n :=
  density_empty.symm.trans_le <|
    le_csSup ⟨1, by rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩; exact density_le_one X⟩ ⟨∅, isPacking_empty, rfl⟩

/-- The lattice packing constant is at most the sphere packing constant. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem latticePackingDensity_le_spherePackingDensity (n : ℕ) :
    latticePackingDensity n ≤ spherePackingDensity n := by
  refine Real.sSup_le ?_ (spherePackingDensity_nonneg n)
  rintro _ ⟨X, ⟨hX, -⟩, rfl⟩
  exact le_csSup ⟨1, by rintro _ ⟨Y, -, rfl⟩; exact density_le_one Y⟩ ⟨X, hX, rfl⟩

/-- **Conway–Sloane conjecture** [Sl98, CS95]. In every dimension $n \le 9$, the densest sphere
packing is a lattice packing: $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$. The cases $n = 1, 2, 3, 8$ are known
(Thue, Fejes Tóth, Hales, Viazovska); the cases $n = 4, 5, 6, 7$ assert that the lattices
$D_4$, $D_5$, $E_6$, $E_7$ are optimal among all packings, and the case $n = 9$ asserts that
the (unknown) optimal packing density is attained by a lattice, conjecturally $\Lambda_9$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing :
    ∀ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 9, spherePackingDensity n = latticePackingDensity n := by
  sorry

/-- The sphere packing constant in dimension `8` is $\pi^4 / 384$, attained by the $E_8$ lattice
[Vi17]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_eight : spherePackingDensity 8 = π ^ 4 / 384 := by
  sorry

/-- The sphere packing constant in dimension `24` is $\pi^{12} / 12!$, attained by the Leech
lattice [CKMRV17]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_twenty_four :
    spherePackingDensity 24 = π ^ 12 / (Nat.factorial 12) := by
  sorry

/-- In some dimension $n$ the densest sphere packing is irregular, i.e. no lattice packing is
optimal: $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$. Support comes from dimension `10`, where the densest known
packing (the Best packing $P_{10c}$) is not a lattice packing. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, latticePackingDensity n < spherePackingDensity n := by
  sorry

/-- Lattices are suboptimal in all sufficiently high dimensions [CK09]:
$\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular_eventually :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, latticePackingDensity n < spherePackingDensity n := by
  sorry

/-- **Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound** [TS06, Section 5.4]. For large $n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim 3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}
  = 3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-0.7786524795\ldots n},$$
an exponential improvement on Minkowski's lower bound $2^{-n}$. We state the consequence that
$\Delta_n \ge c \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$ for some constant $c > 0$ and all
sufficiently large $n$. The bound is conditional on the pair-correlation conjecture of
[TS06, Section 5.1] on disordered packings. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) * 2 ^ (-(3 - logb 2 (exp 1)) * n / 2) ≤
        spherePackingDensity n := by
  sorry

/-- A weak form of the Torquato–Stillinger conjecture [TS06]: the sphere packing constant admits
an exponential improvement on Minkowski's lower bound, i.e. $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-(1 - \varepsilon) n}$
for some $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound_weak :
    ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(1 - ε) * n) ≤ spherePackingDensity n := by
  sorry

end SpherePacking

Minor remark: the note for the first slot lists explicit densities for n = 4..7, but Sloane's cited paper states the conjecture uniformly as Δ_n^{(L)} = Δ_n for n ≤ 9, so the formalization follows the uniform statement (the explicit values are consequences given the known Δ_n^{(L)} for n ≤ 8).
modeling_decisions: Packing model: a packing of unit balls in ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is given by its set of centers X with pairwise distance ≥ 2 (`IsPacking`), exactly as in Viazovska (2017) and Cohn–Elkies. Restricting to unit radius loses no generality (scaling preserves density).

Density: `density X = limsup_{R→∞} vol((⋃_{x∈X} ball x 1) ∩ ball 0 R) / vol(ball 0 R)` in ℝ, using `volume.real` and `Filter.limsup` over `atTop` (upper density with origin-centred balls, as in Viazovska/Cohn). The finite densities lie in [0,1] (proved: `finiteDensity_nonneg`, `finiteDensity_le_one`), so the real-valued limsup is a genuine limsup and `density X ≤ 1` (proved). By Groemer's theorem the supremum does not depend on using upper vs. lower density, so Δ_n agrees with the sources' Δ_n / φ_max.

Sphere packing constant `spherePackingDensity n = sSup (density '' {X | IsPacking X})` and lattice constant `latticePackingDensity n = sSup (density '' {X | IsPacking X ∧ IsLattice X})`; both index sets are nonempty (∅ is a packing; scaled ℤ^n is a lattice packing) and bounded above by 1, so the real `sSup` is the true supremum (no junk-value issue). `latticePackingDensity_le_spherePackingDensity` is proved as an API sanity check.

Lattice: `IsLattice X := ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L), IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ X = L` — a full-rank discrete ℤ-submodule (Mathlib's `IsZLattice`). A lattice packing is a packing whose centre set is such a lattice (Sloane: 'any packing in which the centers form a lattice'); translates have the same density, so requiring 0 ∈ X is harmless.

Slot 1 quantifies over `n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 9` rather than all `n ≤ 9`; the excluded case n = 0 is degenerate and provably true anyway (both constants equal 1 in ℝ^0), so the statements are equivalent; the notes' explicit values for n = 4..7 (D4, D5, E6, E7) are not hard-coded, since Sloane states the conjecture uniformly as Δ_n = Δ_n^{(L)}.

Slot 3 uses `∃ c > 0` instead of the truncated decimal leading constant 3.276100896 (which is a numerically determined value 1/(2^{2/3} D_1 √π)); the exponent is kept exact as (3 − log₂ e)/2 via `logb 2 (exp 1)`. This is the consequence of TS's asymptotic '∼' statement and is the form suggested by the decomposition notes. Category kept `research open` (bound is conditional on their Conjecture on pair correlation functions).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sphere packing

This file states conjectures about the optimal density of packings of congruent balls in
Euclidean space. It includes the Conway--Sloane conjecture in the remaining open dimensions at
most nine, the possibility that lattice packings are suboptimal, and the Torquato--Stillinger
conjectural asymptotic lower bound.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [N. J. A. Sloane, *The Sphere-Packing Problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207256)
- [S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, *New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density of
  sphere packings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
-/

namespace SpherePacking

open Filter MeasureTheory

/-- A set of centers of congruent unit balls in Euclidean `n`-space is a sphere packing if
distinct centers are at distance at least two. -/
def IsPacking (n : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  P.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y

/-- The upper density of a unit-sphere packing. It is the limsup, as the radius tends to
infinity, of the number of centers in the ball of that radius, multiplied by the volume of a
unit ball and divided by the volume of the observation ball. -/
noncomputable def packingDensity (n : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun r : ℝ =>
    (P ∩ Metric.ball 0 r).ncard * volume.real (Metric.ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) /
      volume.real (Metric.ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) r)) atTop

/-- A packing is a lattice packing if its center set is a full-rank discrete `ℤ`-submodule of
Euclidean space. -/
def IsLatticePacking (n : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  IsPacking n P ∧
    ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (hL : DiscreteTopology L),
      @IsZLattice ℝ inferInstance (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) inferInstance inferInstance L hL ∧
        P = (L : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))

/-- The supremum of upper densities of all unit-sphere packings in Euclidean `n`-space. -/
noncomputable def optimalPackingDensity (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {d : ℝ | ∃ P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), IsPacking n P ∧ packingDensity n P = d}

/-- The supremum of upper densities of all unit-sphere lattice packings in Euclidean `n`-space. -/
noncomputable def optimalLatticePackingDensity (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {d : ℝ | ∃ P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)),
    IsLatticePacking n P ∧ packingDensity n P = d}

/--
The Conway--Sloane conjecture: in every dimension $1 \le n \le 9$, the supremum of the
densities of all congruent-sphere packings equals the supremum restricted to lattice packings.
The cases $n=1,2,3,8$ are known; the open content is $n=4,5,6,7,9$, and in dimension nine
even the lattice supremum is not known explicitly.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ 9 →
      optimalPackingDensity n = optimalLatticePackingDensity n := by
  sorry

/--
The conjectured possibility of an irregular (that is, non-lattice) optimal sphere packing:
there is a positive dimension $n$ in which the supremum of lattice-packing densities is strictly
less than the supremum over all packings. The use of suprema does not assert that either optimum
is attained.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ optimalLatticePackingDensity n < optimalPackingDensity n := by
  sorry

/--
The Torquato--Stillinger conjectural asymptotic lower bound: for some constant $c>0$ and all
sufficiently large dimensions $n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge c n^{1/6} 2^{-(3-\log_2 e)n/2}.$$
Here $\Delta_n$ is the supremum over all sphere packings, not only lattice packings. This bound
is conditional in their paper on their pair-correlation conjecture.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 6 : ℝ) *
          2 ^ (-((3 - Real.logb 2 (Real.exp 1)) * (n : ℝ) / 2)) ≤
        optimalPackingDensity n := by
  sorry

end SpherePacking
modeling_decisions: Represented a packing of congruent unit balls by its set of centers, with pairwise distance at least 2. Rescaling makes the choice of unit radius immaterial for packing density.

Defined packing density as the upper asymptotic density obtained from center counts in origin-centered Euclidean balls: the limsup of the center count times unit-ball volume divided by observation-ball volume. # Sphere packing

A *sphere packing* in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ of centres such that
distinct points of $X$ are at distance at least $2$, so that the open unit balls centred at the
points of $X$ are pairwise disjoint. The *(upper) density* of the packing is
$$\Delta_X := \limsup_{r \to \infty}
  \frac{\mathrm{vol}\big(\bigcup_{x \in X} B(x, 1) \cap B(0, r)\big)}{\mathrm{vol}(B(0, r))},$$
the *sphere packing constant* $\Delta_n$ is the supremum of $\Delta_X$ over all sphere packings
$X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, and the *lattice sphere packing constant* $\Delta_n^{(L)}$ is the
supremum of $\Delta_X$ over those sphere packings whose set of centres $X$ is a lattice
(a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^n$ of full rank).

The value of $\Delta_n$ is known only for $n = 1, 2, 3, 8, 24$, and $\Delta_n^{(L)}$ is known only
for $n \le 8$ and $n = 24$. This file states the open problems about the remaining dimensions
that are recorded in the Wikipedia article: the Conway–Sloane conjecture that the densest packing
is a lattice packing in all dimensions $n \le 9$, the conjecture that in some dimension the densest
packing is irregular (not a lattice packing), and the Torquato–Stillinger conjectural asymptotic
lower bound on $\Delta_n$ that improves exponentially on Minkowski's bound $2^{-n}$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in

- [S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, *New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density of
  sphere packings*, Exp. Math. 15 (2006), 307–331](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
- [M. Viazovska, *The sphere packing problem in dimension 8*, Ann. of Math. 185 (2017),
  991–1015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04246)
- [H. Cohn, A. Kumar, S. D. Miller, D. Radchenko and M. Viazovska, *The sphere packing problem in
  dimension 24*, Ann. of Math. 185 (2017), 1017–1033](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06518)
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory Metric Real

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Topology

namespace SpherePacking

variable {n : ℕ}

/--
A set `X` of points of `ℝ^n` is the set of centres of a *sphere packing* (by unit balls) if any
two distinct points of `X` are at distance at least `2`. Equivalently, the open unit balls centred
at the points of `X` are pairwise disjoint.
-/
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y

/--
The set of points of `ℝ^n` covered by the sphere packing with set of centres `X`, i.e. the union
of the open unit balls centred at the points of `X`.
-/
def balls (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Set (ℝ^n) :=
  ⋃ x ∈ X, ball x 1

/--
The *(upper) density* of the sphere packing with set of centres `X`:
$$\limsup_{r \to \infty}
  \frac{\mathrm{vol}\big(\bigcup_{x \in X} B(x, 1) \cap B(0, r)\big)}{\mathrm{vol}(B(0, r))}.$$
-/
noncomputable def density (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun r : ℝ => volume.real (balls X ∩ ball 0 r) / volume.real (ball (0 : ℝ^n) r))
    atTop

/--
The *sphere packing constant* $\Delta_n$: the supremum of the densities of all sphere packings
in `ℝ^n`.
-/
noncomputable def packingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ X : {X : Set (ℝ^n) // IsPacking X}, density X.1

/--
A set `X` of points of `ℝ^n` is a *lattice* if it is a discrete additive subgroup of `ℝ^n` that
spans `ℝ^n`, i.e. if it is the `ℤ`-span of a basis of `ℝ^n`.
-/
def IsLattice (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L), IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ X = L

/--
The *lattice sphere packing constant* $\Delta_n^{(L)}$: the supremum of the densities of all
sphere packings in `ℝ^n` whose set of centres is a lattice.
-/
noncomputable def latticePackingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ X : {X : Set (ℝ^n) // IsPacking X ∧ IsLattice X}, density X.1

/-- The empty set is a sphere packing. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isPacking_empty : IsPacking (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) :=
  Set.pairwise_empty _

/-- The `ℤ`-span of a basis of `ℝ^n` is a lattice. -/

theorem isLattice_span_basis (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (ℝ^n)) :
    IsLattice (Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b) : Set (ℝ^n)) :=
  ⟨_, inferInstance, inferInstance, rfl⟩

theorem density_empty : density (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = 0 := by
  simp [density, balls, limsup_const]

packing in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a lattice packing, i.e. $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$.

This is known for $n = 1$ (trivial), $n = 2$ (Thue, Fejes Tóth), $n = 3$ (Hales) and $n = 8$

open for $n = 4, 5, 6, 7$, where the densest lattices $D_4$, $D_5$, $E_6$, $E_7$ have densities

even the densest lattice is unknown (the laminated lattice $\Lambda_9$ is conjectured to be
optimal).

383–403).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing :
    ∀ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 9, packingConstant n = latticePackingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
In some dimension $n$ the densest sphere packing is irregular, i.e. it is not a lattice packing:
there is $n$ with $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$.

Wikipedia: "it is possible that in some dimensions the densest packing may be irregular. Some
support for this conjecture comes from the fact that in certain dimensions (e.g. 10) the densest
known irregular packing is denser than the densest known regular packing." The evidence in
dimension $10$ is Best's packing $P_{10c}$, which is denser than every known lattice packing in
$\mathbb{R}^{10}$.
-/

theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
A stronger form of `sphere_packing.variants.irregular`, stated by Cohn and Kumar: "It is
conjectured that lattices are suboptimal in all sufficiently high dimensions", i.e.
$\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

*Reference:* H. Cohn and A. Kumar, *Optimality and uniqueness of the Leech lattice among
lattices*, Ann. of Math. 170 (2009), Section 1.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular_eventually :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
The **Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound** on the sphere packing constant: for large
$n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim \frac{3.276100896\, n^{1/6}}{2^{0.7786524795\ldots\, n}},$$
where the exponent is exactly $\tfrac{1}{2}\big(3 - \log_2 e\big) = 0.7786524795\ldots$. In
particular there is a constant $c > 0$ such that
$$\Delta_n \ge c\, n^{1/6}\, 2^{-\frac{3 - \log_2 e}{2} n}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$. This would be an exponential improvement on Minkowski's lower
bound $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-n}$. Torquato and Stillinger derive this bound from their Conjecture 1
on pair correlation functions of disordered sphere packings in high dimensions; the bound
remains unproved.

*Reference:* S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, *New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal
density of sphere packings*, Exp. Math. 15 (2006), 307–331, Abstract and Section 5.3.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) * 2 ^ (-((3 - logb 2 (exp 1)) / 2) * n) ≤
        packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
A weak form of `sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound`: the sphere packing
constant $\Delta_n$ improves exponentially on Minkowski's lower bound $2^{-n}$, i.e. there is
$\varepsilon > 0$ with $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound_weak :
    ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(1 - ε) * n) ≤ packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
**Viazovska's theorem**: the sphere packing constant in dimension $8$ is
$\Delta_8 = \pi^4 / 384$, the density of the $E_8$ lattice packing.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_eight : packingConstant 8 = π ^ 4 / 384 := by
  sorry

/--
The theorem of Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko and Viazovska: the sphere packing constant in
dimension $24$ is $\Delta_{24} = \pi^{12} / 12!$, the density of the Leech lattice packing.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_twenty_four :
    packingConstant 24 = π ^ 12 / (Nat.factorial 12) := by
  sorry

end SpherePacking

One remark: the Torquato–Stillinger bound is a conjectural bound derived from a heuristic Conjecture 1 rather than a conjecture stated as a theorem by the authors; formalizing the resulting inequality (as the table prescribes) is the only faithful Prop-level reading, and the docstring records that it is conditional on their Conjecture 1.
modeling_decisions: Sphere packings are modelled by their set of centres X ⊆ ℝ^n (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) with pairwise distances ≥ 2 (unit balls), exactly as in Viazovska (arXiv:1603.04246) and Cohn (arXiv:1611.01685). Density is the upper density limsup_{r→∞} vol(⋃_{x∈X} B(x,1) ∩ B(0,r))/vol(B(0,r)) (open balls; closed vs open makes no difference), and Δ_n is the supremum of these upper densities over all packings — the standard 'generous' definition; by Groemer's theorem it coincides with the usual one.

Lattice packing constant Δ_n^{(L)} is defined as the supremum of the same density over packings whose centre set is a lattice (Mathlib's `IsZLattice ℝ L` for a discrete `Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)`). Since scaling a lattice to minimal norm exactly 2 does not change its packing density, this supremum equals the classical Δ_n^{(L)} = sup_L V_n (μ/2)^n / covol(L); no separate covolume formula is needed.

Real-valued `limsup` and `⨆` are used. Junk values are not reachable: for r > 0 the ratio lies in [0,1], so the ℝ-limsup is a genuine limsup in [0,1]; the ranges of the suprema are nonempty (∅ is a packing; the ℤ-span of any basis with minimal norm ≥ 2 is a lattice packing) and bounded by 1, so `⨆` is a genuine supremum. A reviewer may want to double check this reasoning or prefer an ℝ≥0∞-valued variant.

`sphere_packing` is restricted to 1 ≤ n ≤ 9 (`Finset.Icc 1 9`); dimension 0 is degenerate (ℝ^0 is a point, both constants equal 1) and not a 'dimension' in the source's sense. The known cases n = 1,2,3,8 are included, matching Sloane's 'for n ≤ 9'.

- the Conway–Sloane conjecture $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for $n \le 9$,
- the conjecture that in some dimension the densest packing is not a lattice packing

- the Torquato–Stillinger conjectural asymptotic lower bound

- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a packing of unit balls if any
two distinct points of `X` are at distance at least $2$. Since density is invariant under scaling,
fixing the radius to be $1$ loses no generality. -/
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y

/-- The set of centres `X` forms a lattice, that is, a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^n$
spanning $\mathbb{R}^n$. -/
def IsLattice (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L), IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ X = L

/-- The union of the unit balls centred at the points of `X`. -/
def balls (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Set (ℝ^n) :=
  ⋃ x ∈ X, Metric.ball x 1

/-- The (upper) density of the packing of unit balls with centres `X`: the limit superior, as
$R \to \infty$, of the fraction of the ball of radius $R$ about the origin that is covered by
the balls of the packing. This is the definition used in [Vi17]. -/

  limsup (fun R : ℝ =>
    (volume (balls X ∩ Metric.ball 0 R)).toReal / (volume (Metric.ball (0 : ℝ^n) R)).toReal)

/-- $\Delta_n$, the supremum of the densities of all packings of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^n$. -/

  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X})

$\mathbb{R}^n$ whose centres form a lattice. -/

  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X ∧ IsLattice X})

This file states conjectures about the maximal density of packings of congruent
spheres in Euclidean space and the maximal density when the centers must form a lattice.

- [Wikipedia, *Sphere packing*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal Topology

namespace SpherePacking

/-- A unit-diameter sphere packing in `d` dimensions, represented by its set of centers. -/
def IsPacking (d : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  P.Pairwise fun x y ↦ 1 ≤ dist x y

/-- A lattice sphere packing is a packing whose centers are the integer span of a real basis. -/
def IsLatticePacking (d : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  IsPacking d P ∧ ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    P = {x | ∃ z : Fin d → ℤ, x = ∑ i, (z i : ℝ) • b i}

/-- The volume of a `d`-dimensional open ball of radius `r`. -/
noncomputable def ballVolume (d : ℕ) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (volume (Metric.ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) r)).toReal

/--
The upper density of a unit-diameter sphere packing, computed in balls centered at the origin.
The packed region is the union of the open radius-`1 / 2` balls around the centers. Taking a
limsup makes the definition applicable when the asymptotic density does not exist.
-/
noncomputable def packingDensity (d : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun r : ℝ ↦
    (volume ((⋃ x : P, Metric.ball (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (1 / 2)) ∩
      Metric.ball 0 r)).toReal / ballVolume d r) atTop

/-- The supremum of the densities of all sphere packings in dimension `d`. -/
noncomputable def optimalDensity (d : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {δ | ∃ P, IsPacking d P ∧ packingDensity d P = δ}

/-- The supremum of the densities of all lattice sphere packings in dimension `d`. -/
noncomputable def optimalLatticeDensity (d : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup {δ | ∃ P, IsLatticePacking d P ∧ packingDensity d P = δ}

/--
**Conway--Sloane sphere-packing conjecture.** In every dimension $1 \le n \le 9$, the
supremum of the densities of all congruent-sphere packings equals the corresponding supremum
for lattice packings. The unresolved dimensions are $4,5,6,7,$ and $9$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ 9 → optimalDensity n = optimalLatticeDensity n := by
  sorry

**Irregular-packing conjecture.** In some positive dimension, non-lattice packings are strictly
better than lattice packings: the supremum over lattice-packing densities is strictly less than
the supremum over all packing densities. Here “irregular” means non-lattice; neither supremum is
asserted to be attained.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ optimalLatticeDensity n < optimalDensity n := by
  sorry

sufficiently large dimensions $n$, the maximal density $\Delta_n$ of arbitrary sphere packings
satisfies

-/

theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,

          Real.rpow 2 (-((3 - Real.logb 2 (Real.exp 1)) / 2) * n) ≤ optimalDensity n := by
  sorry

/-!
# Sphere packing

The sphere packing problem asks for the largest fraction $\Delta_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that can be
covered by non-overlapping congruent balls. The value of $\Delta_n$ is known only for
$n = 1, 2, 3, 8, 24$. Its exact value in the remaining dimensions and its asymptotic behaviour as
$n \to \infty$ are open.

This file defines the sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$ and the lattice sphere packing constant
$\Delta_n^{(L)}$ (the supremum over packings whose centres form a lattice), and states the following
conjectures.

- The Conway–Sloane conjecture that $\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for all $n \le 9$.
- The conjecture that in some dimension the densest packing is irregular, i.e.
  $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$ for some $n$, and the stronger form of Cohn–Kumar that this
  holds for all sufficiently large $n$.
- The Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound
  $\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim 3.276\ldots \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$, an
  exponential improvement on Minkowski's bound $2^{-n}$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sphere packing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sl98] N. J. A. Sloane, *The Sphere-Packing Problem*, Documenta Mathematica, Extra Volume ICM
  1998, III, 387–396. [arXiv:math/0207256](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207256)
- [CoSl95] J. H. Conway and N. J. A. Sloane, *What are all the best sphere packings in low
  dimensions?*, Discrete Comput. Geom. 13 (1995), 383–403.
- [CoKu09] H. Cohn and A. Kumar, *Optimality and uniqueness of the Leech lattice among lattices*,
  Annals of Mathematics 170 (2009), 1003–1050.
  [arXiv:math/0403263](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0403263)
- [ToSt06] S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, *New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density
  of sphere packings*, Experimental Mathematics 15 (2006), 307–331.
  [arXiv:math/0508381](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
- [Vi17] M. Viazovska, *The sphere packing problem in dimension 8*, Annals of Mathematics 185
  (2017), 991–1015. [arXiv:1603.04246](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.04246)
- [CKMRV17] H. Cohn, A. Kumar, S. D. Miller, D. Radchenko and M. Viazovska, *The sphere packing
  problem in dimension 24*, Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), 1017–1033.
  [arXiv:1603.06518](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.06518)

open MeasureTheory Metric Filter Real
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace SpherePacking

variable {n : ℕ}

/--
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a (unit) sphere packing if any two
distinct points of `X` are at distance at least `2`, i.e. the open unit balls centred at the points
of `X` are pairwise disjoint. Since the packing density is invariant under scaling, fixing the
radius to be `1` loses no generality.
-/
def IsPacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  X.Pairwise fun x y => 2 ≤ dist x y

/--
A set `X` of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of centres of a lattice sphere packing if it is
the set of centres of a sphere packing and it is a (full rank) lattice in $\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. a
discrete additive subgroup spanning $\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
def IsLatticePacking (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  IsPacking X ∧
    ∃ (L : Submodule ℤ (ℝ^n)) (_ : DiscreteTopology L),
      IsZLattice ℝ L ∧ (L : Set (ℝ^n)) = X

/--
The finite density of the packing with centres `X` at radius `r`: the fraction of the ball of
radius `r` around the origin that is covered by the open unit balls centred at the points of `X`.
-/
noncomputable def finiteDensity (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (volume ((⋃ x ∈ X, ball x 1) ∩ ball 0 r)).toReal / (volume (ball (0 : ℝ^n) r)).toReal

/--
The density of the packing with centres `X`, defined as the limit superior of the finite densities
as the radius tends to infinity, as in [Vi17].
-/
noncomputable def density (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : ℝ :=
  limsup (finiteDensity X) atTop

/--
The sphere packing constant $\Delta_n$: the supremum of the densities of all sphere packings in
$\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
noncomputable def packingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsPacking X})

/--
The lattice sphere packing constant $\Delta_n^{(L)}$: the supremum of the densities of all lattice
sphere packings in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
-/
noncomputable def latticePackingConstant (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (density '' {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X})

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem finiteDensity_nonneg (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : 0 ≤ finiteDensity X r := by
  unfold finiteDensity
  positivity

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem finiteDensity_le_one (X : Set (ℝ^n)) (r : ℝ) : finiteDensity X r ≤ 1 :=
  div_le_one_of_le₀
    (ENNReal.toReal_mono measure_ball_lt_top.ne (measure_mono Set.inter_subset_right))
    ENNReal.toReal_nonneg

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem density_nonneg (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : 0 ≤ density X :=
  le_limsup_of_frequently_le (Frequently.of_forall (finiteDensity_nonneg X))
    (isBoundedUnder_of ⟨1, finiteDensity_le_one X⟩)

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem density_le_one (X : Set (ℝ^n)) : density X ≤ 1 :=
  limsup_le_of_le (isCoboundedUnder_le_of_le _ (finiteDensity_nonneg X))
    (Eventually.of_forall (finiteDensity_le_one X))

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isPacking_empty : IsPacking (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) :=
  Set.pairwise_empty _

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem density_empty : density (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = 0 := by
  have : finiteDensity (∅ : Set (ℝ^n)) = fun _ => 0 := by
    ext r
    simp [finiteDensity]
  rw [density, this, limsup_const]

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem packingConstant_nonneg (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ packingConstant n :=
  le_csSup_of_le ⟨1, by rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩; exact density_le_one X⟩
    ⟨∅, isPacking_empty, rfl⟩ (density_nonneg _)

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem packingConstant_le_one (n : ℕ) : packingConstant n ≤ 1 :=
  csSup_le ⟨_, ∅, isPacking_empty, rfl⟩ (by rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩; exact density_le_one X)

/-- Every lattice packing is a packing, so $\Delta_n^{(L)} \le \Delta_n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 11 52]
theorem latticePackingConstant_le_packingConstant (n : ℕ) :
    latticePackingConstant n ≤ packingConstant n := by
  by_cases h : ∃ X : Set (ℝ^n), IsLatticePacking X
  · refine csSup_le_csSup ⟨1, ?_⟩ (h.elim fun X hX => ⟨_, X, hX, rfl⟩)
      (Set.image_mono fun X hX => hX.1)
    rintro _ ⟨X, -, rfl⟩
    exact density_le_one X
  · push_neg at h
    have : {X : Set (ℝ^n) | IsLatticePacking X} = ∅ := Set.eq_empty_of_forall_notMem h
    simp only [latticePackingConstant, this, Set.image_empty, Real.sSup_empty]
    exact packingConstant_nonneg n

**Conway–Sloane conjecture** [CoSl95], [Sl98]: for every $n \le 9$ the densest sphere packing in
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is no denser than the densest lattice packing, i.e.
$\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for all $n \le 9$.

$1, 2, 3, 8$ and $24$, where it is a lattice packing, so the conjecture is known for
$n = 1, 2, 3, 8$ and open for $n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 9$. In the open cases $n = 4, 5, 6, 7$ the
conjecture asserts that $\Delta_n$ equals the density of $D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7$ respectively, namely
$\pi^2/16$, $\pi^2/(15\sqrt{2})$, $\pi^3/(48\sqrt{3})$, $\pi^3/105$.
-/

theorem sphere_packing (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 9) :
    packingConstant n = latticePackingConstant n := by
  sorry

It is possible that in some dimension the densest sphere packing is irregular (that is, not a
lattice packing): there is some $n$ with $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$.

Some support for this comes from dimension $10$, where the densest known packing, the
non-lattice packing $P_{10c}$ of Best, is denser than the densest known lattice packing.
-/

theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by

dimensions, i.e. $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/

theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular_high_dimensions :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by
  sorry

**Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound** [ToSt06]: for large $n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim \frac{3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6}}{2^{0.7786524795\ldots n}},$$
where the exponent is exactly $(3 - \log_2 e)/2$. This would be an exponential improvement on
Minkowski's lower bound $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-n}$ and is conditional on the conjecture of [ToSt06]
characterising the pair correlation functions of disordered sphere packings in high dimensions.

Since the leading constant is only determined numerically, we state the bound with an unspecified
positive constant $c$: there is $c > 0$ such that
$\Delta_n \ge c \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) * 2 ^ (-((3 - logb 2 (exp 1)) * n / 2)) ≤
        packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
A weaker form of the Torquato–Stillinger conjecture [ToSt06]: the sphere packing constant admits
an exponential improvement on Minkowski's lower bound $2^{-n}$, i.e. there is $\varepsilon > 0$
such that $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.exponential_improvement :
    ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((1 - ε) * n)) ≤ packingConstant n := by
  sorry

/--
**Kepler conjecture**, proved by Hales [Ha05]: $\Delta_3 = \pi / \sqrt{18}$, the density of the
face-centred cubic lattice packing.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_three :
    packingConstant 3 = π / √18 := by
  sorry

/--
Viazovska [Vi17]: $\Delta_8 = \pi^4 / 384$, the density of the $E_8$ lattice packing.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_eight :
    packingConstant 8 = π ^ 4 / 384 := by
  sorry

/--
Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko and Viazovska [CKMRV17]: $\Delta_{24} = \pi^{12} / 12!$, the
density of the Leech lattice packing.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.dimension_twenty_four :
    packingConstant 24 = π ^ 12 / Nat.factorial 12 := by
  sorry

end SpherePacking

statement_blocks.sphere_packing:
/--
**Conway–Sloane conjecture** [CoSl95], [Sl98]: for every $n \le 9$ the densest sphere packing in
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is no denser than the densest lattice packing, i.e.
$\Delta_n = \Delta_n^{(L)}$ for all $n \le 9$.

The densest lattice packings are known for $n \le 8$ (Blichfeldt: the root lattices
$A_1, A_2, A_3, D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7, E_8$) and for $n = 24$ (the Leech lattice, [CoKu09]), and
$\Delta_9^{(L)}$ is unknown. The optimal packing among all packings is known only in dimensions
$1, 2, 3, 8$ and $24$, where it is a lattice packing, so the conjecture is known for
$n = 1, 2, 3, 8$ and open for $n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 9$. In the open cases $n = 4, 5, 6, 7$ the
conjecture asserts that $\Delta_n$ equals the density of $D_4, D_5, E_6, E_7$ respectively, namely
$\pi^2/16$, $\pi^2/(15\sqrt{2})$, $\pi^3/(48\sqrt{3})$, $\pi^3/105$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 9) :
    packingConstant n = latticePackingConstant n := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.sphere_packing.variants.irregular:
/--
It is possible that in some dimension the densest sphere packing is irregular (that is, not a
lattice packing): there is some $n$ with $\Delta_n^{(L)} < \Delta_n$.

Some support for this comes from dimension $10$, where the densest known packing, the
non-lattice packing $P_{10c}$ of Best, is denser than the densest known lattice packing.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, latticePackingConstant n < packingConstant n := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillin:
/--
**Torquato–Stillinger conjectural lower bound** [ToSt06]: for large $n$,
$$\Delta_n \ge \phi_* \sim \frac{3.276100896 \cdot n^{1/6}}{2^{0.7786524795\ldots n}},$$
where the exponent is exactly $(3 - \log_2 e)/2$. This would be an exponential improvement on
Minkowski's lower bound $\Delta_n \ge 2^{-n}$ and is conditional on the conjecture of [ToSt06]
characterising the pair correlation functions of disordered sphere packings in high dimensions.

Since the leading constant is only determined numerically, we state the bound with an unspecified
positive constant $c$: there is $c > 0$ such that
$\Delta_n \ge c \cdot n^{1/6} \cdot 2^{-(3 - \log_2 e) n / 2}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6) * 2 ^ (-((3 - logb 2 (exp 1)) * n / 2)) ≤
        packingConstant n := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil
import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.ZLattice.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.VolumeOfBalls

/-!
# Sphere packing

This file states conjectures about the optimal density of packings of congruent spheres in
Euclidean space. A packing is represented by its set of centers, with unit spheres having disjoint
interiors. Its upper density is the limsup of the proportion of an expanding ball occupied by the
unit spheres.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, "Sphere packing"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing)
- [N. J. A. Sloane, "The Sphere-Packing Problem" (1998)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0207256)
- [S. Torquato and F. H. Stillinger, "New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density of
  sphere packings" (2006)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508381)
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory Module
open scoped ENNReal Topology

namespace SpherePacking

/-- A packing of open unit balls in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, represented by their centers. -/
def IsPacking (n : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  P.Pairwise fun x y ↦ 2 ≤ dist x y

/-- The upper density of the open unit balls centered at `P`, measured in balls about the origin. -/
noncomputable def upperDensity (n : ℕ) (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  atTop.limsup fun k : ℕ ↦
    volume (Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) k ∩
      ⋃ x ∈ P, Metric.ball x 1) /
      volume (Metric.closedBall (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) k)

/-- The supremum of upper densities of all unit-sphere packings in dimension `n`. -/
noncomputable def optimalDensity (n : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (_ : IsPacking n P), upperDensity n P

/-- The supremum of upper densities of unit-sphere packings whose centers form a full lattice. -/
noncomputable def optimalLatticeDensity (n : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (b : Basis (Fin n) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (_ : IsPacking n (Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b))),
      upperDensity n (Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b))

/--
The Conway--Sloane low-dimensional sphere-packing conjecture: in every positive dimension at most
$9$, the supremum of densities of all sphere packings equals the supremum restricted to lattice
packings. The open cases are dimensions $4,5,6,7$, and $9$; the other cases in this range are known.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem sphere_packing :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ 9 → optimalDensity n = optimalLatticeDensity n := by
  sorry

/--
Some dimension has genuinely irregular (non-lattice) sphere packings: the supremum of lattice
packing densities is strictly smaller than the supremum over all sphere packings in that dimension.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.irregular :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ optimalLatticeDensity n < optimalDensity n := by
  sorry

/--
The Torquato--Stillinger conjectural asymptotic lower bound: for some constant $c>0$ and all
sufficiently large dimensions $n$,
$$\Delta_n \geq c n^{1/6} 2^{-(3-\log_2 e)n/2}.$$
Here `optimalDensity n` is the supremum over all, not merely lattice, sphere packings.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51]
theorem sphere_packing.variants.torquato_stillinger_lower_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ENNReal.ofReal
          (c * Real.rpow n (1 / 6) /
            Real.rpow 2 (((3 - Real.logb 2 (Real.exp 1)) * n) / 2)) ≤
        optimalDensity n := by
  sorry

end SpherePacking
modeling_decisions: A sphere packing in dimension n is represented by a set of centers in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with pairwise center distance at least 2; this normalizes all spheres to unit radius without changing achievable densities.

Packing density is modeled as upper asymptotic occupied-volume density: the limsup, over natural radii tending to infinity, of the volume fraction of an origin-centered closed ball covered by the union of open unit balls. This follows the article's average/asymptotic density language and allows touching spheres while keeping interiors disjoint.
The optimal density is the supremum over all center-set packings, so no attainment of a densest packing is assumed.

A full lattice is represented using Mathlib's characterization as the integer span of a real basis. The lattice optimum is the supremum over basis-generated center sets satisfying the packing condition. Translates are omitted because translating a lattice packing does not change its asymptotic density.

The Conway–Sloane slot is stated for every positive n ≤ 9. This includes the known dimensions 1, 2, 3, and 8 and leaves the intended open content in dimensions 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9; dimension 0 is excluded as degenerate.
The irregular variant uses the strict inequality between the lattice and unrestricted suprema, as required by the decomposition, and explicitly excludes dimension 0.

The Torquato–Stillinger bound is stated in the permitted eventual positive-constant form, with exact exponent (3 − log₂ e)/2 and unrestricted optimal packing density. ENNReal.ofReal embeds the positive real lower-bound expression into the density codomain.
